cards.explanation: The answer is sword and famine and plague. The LORD of Hosts says, “I will send against them sword and famine and plague…” (Jeremiah 29:17). It's aimed at the king and the people still in Jerusalem. I think this is a heavy verse, friends, and it's okay to let it sit for a second.

The answer is that they have not listened to His words. The LORD says, “…they have not listened to My words, declares the LORD…” (Jeremiah 29:19). The text doesn't hand us a second reason, so we won't go looking for one. He sent those words again and again, which makes this verse sting even more.
The answer is prophets. The LORD says His words came “…again and again through My servants the prophets.” (Jeremiah 29:19). He kept sending them, friends. That's a lot of knocking on the same door.

The answer is False, and it's a tough one. The LORD says, “And neither have you exiles listened, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:19). The word “neither” puts the exiles right beside the people in Jerusalem. The LORD isn't only talking about the folks back home.

The answer is the king of Babylon. The LORD says He will deliver Ahab and Zedekiah to “…Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…” (Jeremiah 29:21). The LORD also says Nebuchadnezzar will kill them before the exiles' very eyes, and I think that part is heavy. The LORD says it plainly, so we'll say it plainly too.

The answer is False, because it's not out of sight. The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, “…will kill them before your very eyes.” (Jeremiah 29:21). The exiles will watch it happen. That's a sobering verse, friends, and I think it's meant to be.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I am He who knows, and I am a witness, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:23). He saw the adultery and the lies in His name. Nothing was hidden from Him, and that's a serious thing to read.

The answer is his own name. The LORD says, “In your own name you have sent out letters…” (Jeremiah 29:25). Those letters went to all the people of Jerusalem, to the priest Zephaniah, and to all the priests. Shemaiah sent them in his own name, friends, and I'd say that matters a lot.

The answer is True. In his letter, Shemaiah tells Zephaniah to deal with “…any madman who acts like a prophet—you must put him in stocks and neck irons.” (Jeremiah 29:26). He's pushing Zephaniah, the priest, to act. Shemaiah is the one saying this, not the LORD.

The answer is Jeremiah. Shemaiah writes, “So now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who poses as a prophet among you?” (Jeremiah 29:27). Shemaiah says Jeremiah has sent word to the exiles in Babylon (Jeremiah 29:28). Complaining about him is a bold move, friends.

The answer is lengthy. Shemaiah complains that Jeremiah's message was, “Since the exile will be lengthy, build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat their produce.” (Jeremiah 29:28). The message is about settling in, with houses, gardens and produce.

The answer is that he reads it to Jeremiah. The text says, “Zephaniah the priest, however, had read this letter to Jeremiah the prophet.” (Jeremiah 29:29). The letter that was supposed to get Jeremiah in trouble landed right in front of him. The text doesn't say why Zephaniah did it, so I won't guess.

The answer is False. The LORD says Shemaiah “…has prophesied to you—though I did not send him…” (Jeremiah 29:31). He prophesied without being sent. Showing up with a message is one thing, friends, and being sent with it is another.

The answer is that he made them trust in a lie. The LORD says Shemaiah “…has made you trust in a lie…” (Jeremiah 29:31). The exiles are the ones he made do it. I think it's a sad line, because trust is a big thing to hand to the wrong voice.

The answer is False. The LORD says Shemaiah “…will have no one left among this people, nor will he see the good that I will bring to My people, declares the LORD…” (Jeremiah 29:32). Notice the LORD still speaks of good coming to His people. Shemaiah just won't be there to see it.

The answer is that he preached rebellion against the LORD. That's the reason the verse ends on: “…for he has preached rebellion against the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:32). The verse before adds that Shemaiah prophesied though the LORD did not send him, and made the exiles trust in a lie (Jeremiah 29:31). It's a heavy verse, friends, and a good reminder of how much words can weigh.
